Lessons.Title: Complex Numbers
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning goals: write square roots of negative reals in terms of i, plot complex coordinates, add/subtract and multiply/divide complex numbers.
The imaginary unit i satisfies i²=−1. A complex number is a+bi with independently real and imaginary coefficients.
Complex numbers form ordered-coordinate points (real,imaginary) in the plane. Addition is component-wise and subtraction reverses each component of the subtrahend.
Multiply using distribution and i²=−1. For a quotient, multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate of a nonzero complex denominator.
The powers of i cycle every four. To evaluate complex-valued functions, substitute and simplify algebraically, checking that original rational denominators are not zero.
Independent Edulytics cool-down: (a) Plot z=−3+2i. (b) Compute (2−i)(3+2i). (c) Simplify (3+i)/(1−i). (d) Find i^26.
Independent Try It 1 — Negative-root conversion. Simplify √(−48).
Independent Try It 2 — Complex coordinate plotting. Plot 4−5i on complex axes.
Independent Try It 3 — Complex subtraction. Find (5+2i)−(3−4i).
Independent Try It 4 — Multiply real and complex. Find −2(3+5i).
Independent Try It 5 — Multiply two complex numbers. Find (3−2i)(1+4i).
Independent Try It 6 — Polynomial substitution. Evaluate f(z)=z²−z at z=3−i.
Independent Try It 7 — Rational substitution. Evaluate (z+1)/(z−2) at z=i.

KeyConcepts.Title: Complex plane
KeyConcepts.Rule: Horizontal axis real; vertical axis imaginary.

KeyConcepts.Title: Addition/subtraction
KeyConcepts.Definition: Combine real parts and imaginary parts separately.

KeyConcepts.Title: Complex quotient
KeyConcepts.Definition: Multiply numerator and denominator by denominator conjugate.
KeyConcepts.Rule: A nonzero complex denominator gives a positive real a²+b².

KeyConcepts.Title: Complex substitution
KeyConcepts.Definition: Polynomial/rational functions may accept complex inputs if denominators are nonzero.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Use complex multiplication and conjugates to simplify.

Visuals.Title: Complex coordinate pairs
Visuals.Description: Independent mapping from standard form to the Argand plane.

Visuals.Title: Cyclic imaginary powers
Visuals.Description: The values repeat every four exponent steps.

SummaryPoints: Complex arithmetic combines real and imaginary components.

CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Real axis is horizontal and imaginary vertical.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Dividing real and imaginary parts term by term.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Complex denominator must be handled as a whole.
